deep.reconstruction:
This page is part of the outline (pp. 2-4) for Grothendieck's Nov-Dec 1967 IHES talks on crystals. Those talks were later written up by Coates and Jussila as 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968). The page continues point 4, the 'metaphysical consequences' of the comparison theorem H^*_DR(X) ≅ H^*(X^an, C) for X smooth over C. Transcendentally defined complex cohomology has a purely algebraic description, the hypercohomology of the algebraic de Rham complex Ω^•_{X/k}. This description makes sense for smooth schemes over any field. It carries the Hodge filtration, whose graded pieces are the E_∞ terms of the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence E_1^{pq} = H^q(X, Ω^p) ⇒ H^{p+q}_DR(X).

Point 5 is a critique of de Rham cohomology as a universal cohomology. Item (a) is struck out; it mentioned a good duality theory, cycle classes, and a reference to Hodge and a Bourbaki exposé, and was replaced by a note on the char p case. Item (b) says that in characteristic 0, for complete smooth varieties, de Rham cohomology gives excellent invariants, in particular the right Betti numbers. In characteristic p it is less reasonable, for three reasons:
(1) For X not proper the groups are infinite-dimensional. For example H^0_DR(X) = ker(d: O_X → Ω^1) equals Γ(X, O_X^p) by Cartier's theorem, and for affine smooth X = Spec A this is A^p.
(2) Even for X proper, dim H^1_DR need not be the 'right' b_1. One has dim H^1_DR ≥ 2 dim Pic, with strict inequality in examples, attributed to p-torsion phenomena (non-reduced Picard schemes and torsion in crystalline cohomology; Igusa and Mumford type examples).
(3) Even when the dimensions are right, as for abelian varieties, the coefficients lie in a field of characteristic p (a remark credited to Serre). So Lefschetz trace formulas compute fixed-point numbers only mod p, and de Rham cohomology cannot give a satisfactory formulation of the Weil conjectures.

A struck-out marginal note asks whether de Rham theory lives up to the general (six-operations-type) formalisms one is now used to, apparently 'with respect to Henselized sites'. The next page continues with a further defect: de Rham cohomology fails for singular varieties, e.g. a nodal curve. This motivates crystalline and infinitesimal cohomology.
errors: The inequality is transcribed as dim H^1_DR(X) ≥ 2 dim Pic_X. The correct general statement for proper smooth X is dim H^1_DR ≥ b_1 = 2 dim (Pic^0_X)_red. Read with Pic meaning the Picard variety, the statement is correct.

The identification H^0_DR(X) ≅ H^0(X, O_X)^p requires X smooth over a perfect field (via the Cartier isomorphism) and holds only as an abelian group or Frobenius-twisted k-space. The text leaves this implicit; in an outline that is harmless.

ideas.what: Algebraic de Rham cohomology as an algebraic description of complex cohomology, valid over any field, with the Hodge filtration coming from the Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic de Rham cohomology / Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966, 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties', Publ. IHES 29)
ideas.where_published: Publ. Math. IHES 29 (1966); Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Defects of de Rham cohomology in char p: infinite dimension in the non-proper case (Cartier), wrong b_1 because of p-torsion and non-reduced Pic, and characteristic-p coefficients making Lefschetz formulas valid only mod p (Serre)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Serre; examples by Igusa and Mumford
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, §1-2 (Dix exposés, 1968)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a lecture outline whose content matches the published introduction to 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1968). Only the struck-out marginal query about a six-operations formalism relative to (Henselized?) sites is unpublished, and it is too fragmentary to carry content.
transcription_corrections: The margin note beside 5b) reads approximately '{+pour coh. DR. des variétés complètes lisses+}' and is inserted after 'pour la'. The transcription has this right.

Struck-out item a) seems to begin 'Bonne théorie de dualité ...' with an inserted '[le cas car p (loc. ...)]'. A second line mentions 'classes associées à des cycles (cf ... Hodge, dans mon exposé[?] Bourbaki)'. It is largely illegible.

Struck-out margin: 'Mais on sait qu'elle n'est pas à la hauteur des formalismes généraux dans les pp.[?] auxquels on est maintenant habitué. Un tel formalisme, par rapport aux sites [Hensélisés?], devrait avoir ...'. The word read as 'Hensélisés' is very uncertain.
Line 4 reads 'E_∞ associé à une suite spectrale (*). Voir [peut-être 'Voir par' = 'Voir pour'] des commentaires sur papier bleu'.
